introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, N = 14.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The table below shows some elements on the Periodic Table. The letters are not the usual symbols of the elements.

| Element | Mass Number | Atomic number | Proton number | Neutron number | Electron number |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 35 | 17 | 17 | **X** | **Y** |
| B | 24 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| C | **Z** | 3 | 3 | 4 | 3 |
| D | 16 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
incertitudes: Points imprimés 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 10, conformes au total. Le tableau est recopié avec les inconnues X, Y et Z en gras comme dans le sujet.

En-tête de la Section A : « ANSWER ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 answers » ; modélisé en « 4 sur 5 » (toutes tentées, 4 meilleures notées). Section B : « ANSWER ALL 2 questions » modélisé en « 2 sur 2 ». Section C : « ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3 » (si plus de 2 tentées, seules les deux premières comptent) ; modélisé en « 2 sur 3 ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the table above by giving the values of

(i) **X** .........

(ii) **Y** .........

(iii) **Z** ......... *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Neutron number = mass number - proton number, so $X = 35 - 17 = \mathbf{18}$.

(ii) A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, so $Y = \mathbf{17}$.

(iii) Mass number = protons + neutrons, so $Z = 3 + 4 = \mathbf{7}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Elements A and B are involved in bonding.

(i) Give the formula of the compound formed. .........

(ii) Name the type of bond involved. ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Element A has 17 protons, so it is **chlorine (Cl)**; element B has 12 protons, so it is **magnesium (Mg)**.

(i) Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses 2 electrons to form $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$; each chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) gains 1 electron to form $\mathrm{Cl^-}$. Two chloride ions are needed for one magnesium ion: the formula is **$\mathrm{MgCl_2}$**.

(ii) The bond is an **ionic (electrovalent) bond**, formed by the transfer of electrons from the metal to the non-metal.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the electronic configuration of elements

(i) A .........

(ii) D ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A has 17 electrons: **2, 8, 7**.

(ii) D has 8 electrons: **2, 6**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
To which group of the Periodic Table do elements C and D fall?

(i) C .........

(ii) D ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) C has atomic number 3 (lithium), electronic configuration 2, 1: one outer electron, so it is in **Group I** (the alkali metals).

(ii) D has atomic number 8 (oxygen), electronic configuration 2, 6: six outer electrons, so it is in **Group VI** (Group 16).

questions.enonce_markdown: How would the element C be stored in the laboratory? ......... *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: C is lithium, an alkali metal that reacts with the oxygen and the moisture of the air. It is stored **under oil (paraffin oil or kerosene)**.
